content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [SEV-2] gpu-queue growth detected for gpu-eu-west pool. queue length > 500 and average request latency > 3s. Autoscaler reports "max nodes reached" for nodepool gpu-eu-west-1-pool. See metrics: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/gpu-queue

Alice Chen: ack, I'm oncall. Checking nodepool status and quota now. pinging infra.

oncall-sre: Paging Alice Chen (oncall). Please confirm if this is customer impacting.

Alice Chen: Javier, can you confirm user-facing error rate?

Javier Gomez: Seeing 503s for Gen API on hosted (eu-west). Error rate up ~2.8% over baseline, spike started ~5m ago. Several customers reporting slow responses. Queue backlog ~720. Customer-impacting for high-throughput tenants.

Omar Patel: Confirmed from infra side: ClusterAutoscaler annotated desired=28 but max=28 for gpu-eu-west-1-pool. Attempts to scale up are being rejected. Cloud quota looks fine for raw GPUs, but our nodepool max constraint is at tf var gpu_pool_max_nodes=28.

Mei Lin: This matches the runbook for "nodepool max hit". Short-term options: 1) increase pool max and trigger terraform apply (fast if infra has pre-approved automation), 2) spin up a temporary emergency pool and migrate pods, 3) evict lower-priority jobs. Recommend immediate manual bump to unblock traffic, then followup with postmortem. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/scale-unblock

Alice Chen: I will do option 1 if infra approves. Omar, can you give the quick thumbs? :thumbsup:

Omar Patel: Thumbs. We have spare quota in the account. Suggest bump to 40 nodes to handle the current backlog and give headroom for 30m. I'll watch GPU provisioning.

Alice Chen: Executing manual cap raise now. Pasting command used by infra-automation:

```
# temporary emergency bump
terraform workspace select production
terraform apply -var 'gpu_pool_max_nodes=40' -target=module.gpu_eu_west.node_pool -auto-approve
```

infra-runbot: Starting terraform apply for module.gpu_eu_west.node_pool. Plan: update var gpu_pool_max_nodes: 28 -> 40.

infra-runbot: Apply complete. New max nodes for gpu-eu-west-1-pool: 40. (request id infra-apply-2026-04-12-01)

incident-bot: Noted cluster autoscaler will re-evaluate. Next check in ~30s.

Mei Lin: Triggering ClusterAutoscaler resync: `kubectl annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler redwood/invalidate-eviction=ts-$(date +%s)` (internal helper).

infra-runbot: CA resync acknowledged. Provisioning 8 additional nodes (gpu type a100). Expected startup ~4-7m.

Javier Gomez: Early signs: queue length down to 420, 503s trending down. Customers still seeing elevated latency but improving.

Alice Chen: Monitoring logs/metrics. Initiating emergency mitigation checklist item: reduce test job priority to free slots if needed.

Mei Lin: Also enabling temporary pod eviction protection for critical services to avoid flapping during scale.

oncall-sre: Are there any blocked pods stuck on scheduling due to pod anti-affinity? Might be worth checking taints/tolerations.

Omar Patel: Good call — found a misconfigured PodDisruptionBudget on rerank-worker that prevented eviction, created scheduling pressure. I've patched it to relax the budget to 80%. Command used: `kubectl patch pdb rerank-worker -p '{"spec":{"minAvailable":1}}'`

infra-runbot: New nodes are ready. Node count for gpu-eu-west-1-pool = 36 -> scaling to 40 requested.

Javier Gomez: Queue now 120, 503s back to baseline ~0.2%. Latency trending to normal.

Alice Chen: Great. Marking incident as mitigated for immediate customer impact. Will keep thread open until backlog fully cleared and autoscaler stable.

Mei Lin: Action items before we close: - create follow-up ticket to increase default max for pool to 50 for EU projects (RDW-INC-2026) - add a guard to auto-escalate when queue > 500 for >5m - update runbook to include poddisruptionbudget check on scale-block cases.

Omar Patel: I'll open the infra RFC to adjust the pool defaults and add a quick quota check in the autoscaler health monitor.

Alice Chen: Filing RDW-INC-2026 and assigning to SRE/Infra. Postmortem owner: Mei Lin. Estimated timeline for writeup: 48h.

Mei Lin: Recommend we also add a temporary automated policy that allows a one-time emergency bump from oncall with a signed approval step to avoid manual terraform runs at 2am.

Alice Chen: Agree. For now, adding note to runbook and flagging product teams that some tenants experienced degraded performance. Javier, please loop in support org for customer comms.

Javier Gomez: Will do. Drafting a customer message and will circulate for approval.

Alice Chen: Closing operational loop: backlog drained, autoscaler functioning, new max set to 40. Keeping thread open for 1h to ensure stability. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
